subject.title: fix(plugins): preserve already-loaded plugins across scoped harness activation

question: Should a harness miss add the missing plugin contribution to the existing process registry, or resolve it through a request-scoped registry handle that never replaces global state?
rationale: Both directions avoid broad re-registration, but choosing the permanent global-versus-request-scoped ownership boundary affects loader, cache, cleanup, and plugin lifecycle semantics beyond this two-file patch.

options.title: Use request-scoped activation
options.body: Resolve the missing harness through a scoped registry handle while leaving the process-global active registry and existing plugin instances untouched.

options.title: Implement additive global activation
options.body: Merge only the newly loaded plugin contribution into the active registry with explicit lifecycle, cleanup, and rollback coverage.

options.title: Approve broad re-registration
options.body: Keep the union approach only after explicitly making repeated plugin registration an accepted contract and proving affected plugin lifecycles are idempotent.

recommendation.title: Use request-scoped activation
recommendation.body: Resolve the missing harness through a scoped registry handle while leaving the process-global active registry and existing plugin instances untouched.

likelyOwner.reason: The runtime-owned harness work in commit `35a412c` is the closest feature-history ownership signal for this lifecycle choice.
